B"H

# Phase 1 — Boundless Brainstorm

The Awtsmoos creates the page and request anew; let every hidden failure come into view.
Awtsmoos.com should feel cinematic, coherent, resilient, fast, and true.

## Every Useful Possibility Worth Considering

1. Build a route manifest from real `geelooy` entrypoints instead of hand-maintained guesses.
2. Crawl static pages and follow same-origin links to discover hidden page families.
3. Capture `pageerror`, console error/warn, failed requests, HTTP 4xx/5xx, MIME mismatches, and rejected module imports.
4. Classify browser-extension noise separately from site-owned failures.
5. Add a reusable static-module resolver test that verifies every `script[type=module]` import returns JavaScript MIME.
6. Add a local-asset reference scanner for HTML, CSS `url(...)`, JS imports, favicon, images, fonts, workers, and manifests.
7. Add a server fallback guard so missing static modules never masquerade as JSON API responses.
8. Normalize route/static precedence where API routing can swallow asset paths.
9. Centralize client fetch semantics: timeout, cancellation, content type, JSON parsing, structured errors, and diagnostics.
10. Introduce a shared API result/error contract only if current endpoints already reveal incompatible shapes.
11. Add per-API validation at boundaries rather than trusting untyped body/query values.
12. Separate transport adapters from domain behavior so browser and server logic remain testable.
13. Add request IDs to user-facing API failures where server infrastructure already supports correlation.
14. Remove silent catch blocks and surface useful, safe error messages.
15. Detect duplicate API wrappers and converge them behind focused modules while preserving external signatures.
16. Create route-local CSS layers only when a page truly needs them; shared tokens should live in shared foundations.
17. Establish a cinematic spacing/type/elevation/motion token vocabulary without forcing all pages into one visual theme.
18. Ensure every interactive element has hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, and loading states where applicable.
19. Keep responsive layouts usable at narrow mobile widths, landscape phones, tablets, desktops, and wide cinema displays.
20. Add `prefers-reduced-motion` behavior for transitions and animated backgrounds.
21. Make large-screen UI movie-friendly: measured content width, readable subtitles/captions, controlled contrast, and stable overlays.
22. Audit safe-area insets and fixed controls on mobile browsers.
23. Audit high-DPI imagery and object-fit/crop behavior.
24. Audit dark/light/system color behavior if the app supports themes.
25. Add skeletons or explicit loading surfaces only where real latency exists.
26. Ensure empty states and failure states are fully styled, not browser-default fragments.
27. Eliminate global selectors that accidentally restyle unrelated pages.
28. Prefer scoped route classes/data attributes or CSS modules already natural to the project.
29. Audit z-index layers so menus, dialogs, tooltips, video/canvas surfaces, and devtools never fight.
30. Audit keyboard traversal and escape/close behavior for overlays.
31. Audit form labels, autocomplete, validation messages, and submit-state realism.
32. Audit fetch retries: retry only safe/idempotent operations and cap attempts.
33. Audit caching headers and client cache assumptions for static modules and API JSON.
34. Add smoke fixtures for auth-gated pages so unauthenticated behavior is intentional rather than errorful.
35. If dynamic routes exist, derive representative fixture URLs from code/tests instead of inventing IDs.
36. Validate every public module import graph with syntax/import checks.
37. Search for case-sensitive path bugs that work on macOS but fail on Linux hosting.
38. Search for absolute filesystem paths accidentally embedded in browser code.
39. Search for stale references to renamed files, legacy app paths, and duplicated `foundation.js` variants.
40. Check favicon/manifest/social metadata so recurring 404 noise disappears.
41. Check service worker/worker/module paths if present.
42. Check CSP/CORS policies if module or API failures reveal them.
43. Check static server MIME table for `.js`, `.mjs`, `.css`, `.json`, `.wasm`, fonts, and media.
44. Add route-audit output as JSON and human-readable Markdown receipts.
45. Add a regression gate that fails when site-owned console errors or failed requests are found.
46. Run visual screenshots at representative widths for repaired pages.
47. Compare runtime before/after on `/apps` and representative route clusters.
48. Inspect build/deploy scripts for source-vs-generated asset ownership; never edit bundles by hand.
49. Inspect GitHub workflows and hosting config before deployment.
50. Verify the final canonical URL directly after push/deploy.

## Phase 1 Principle

Possibility is Chesed; boundaries are Gevurah; the verified implementation must be Tiferes. Nothing above becomes code merely because it sounds grand. Each item must earn its place through real project evidence.
